stem: A nurse evaluates an adult for classic orthostatic hypotension. Which blood-pressure change meets the standard definition after standing?

options.A: A sustained systolic pressure increase of at least 20 mm Hg within 3 minutes
options.B: A sustained diastolic pressure increase of at least 10 mm Hg within 3 minutes
options.C: Any small decrease in blood pressure immediately after sitting up
options.D: A sustained decrease of at least 20 mm Hg systolic or 10 mm Hg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing

rationale: The American Heart Association scientific statement defines orthostatic hypotension as a sustained reduction in systolic blood pressure of at least 20 mm Hg or diastolic blood pressure of at least 10 mm Hg within 3 minutes of standing. Symptoms may accompany the change but are not required to satisfy the blood-pressure definition. D is correct.
educational_objective: Identify the standard adult blood-pressure threshold used to define classic orthostatic hypotension.
source_document_title: Orthostatic Hypotension in Adults With Hypertension: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
source_locator: Professional Heart Daily — Top Things to Know, item 1: sustained SBP reduction ≥20 mm Hg or DBP ≥10 mm Hg within 3 minutes of standing
source_claim_supported: Classic orthostatic hypotension is defined by a sustained SBP fall of at least 20 mm Hg or DBP fall of at least 10 mm Hg within 3 minutes of standing.

source_original.stem: A nurse evaluates a client for orthostatic hypotension after dizziness on standing. Which blood pressure change meets the standard diagnostic definition in an adult?

options.A: A systolic pressure rise of at least 20 mm Hg within 3 minutes of standing, regardless of whether symptoms occur during the position change.
options.B: A diastolic pressure rise of at least 10 mm Hg within 3 minutes of standing, regardless of whether symptoms occur during the position change.
options.C: Any fall in systolic or diastolic pressure immediately after sitting up, even when the decrease is smaller than established diagnostic thresholds.
options.D: A sustained fall of at least 20 mm Hg systolic or 10 mm Hg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing from a supine position during upright posture.

source_original.rationale: Orthostatic hypotension is defined by a sustained fall in blood pressure of at least 20 mm Hg systolic or 10 mm Hg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing (or head-up tilt) from the supine position. Symptoms can support the clinical assessment but are not required for the blood-pressure criterion.
source_original.source_detail: AHA Scientific Statement, definition section: sustained SBP decrease ≥20 mm Hg or DBP decrease ≥10 mm Hg within 3 minutes of standing. Hypertension. 2024; DOI 10.1161/HYP.0000000000000236; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Moved from a PMC copy to the AHA's official Professional Heart Daily scientific-statement summary, shortened the alternatives, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium. The final item tests the standard threshold without requiring symptoms.

audit_findings.currentness: AHA 2024 scientific statement remains the current cited AHA definition, checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The BP thresholds and 3-minute interval are directly stated by AHA.

distractor_audit.A: Direction is wrong; definition requires a fall.
